call_points.text: SG&A growth will be slower than GP growth, with some increase in Q2 due to increments.
Classic Vacations full-year margin seen at about 2.5%.
Classic platform integration to finish by CY-end; reverse selling from Classic to TBO starts after migration.
Q2 should be somewhat better than Q1 on a QoQ basis, with YoY growth similar outside Middle East.
Cash in bank is ₹1,980-plus crore, against USD 70 million loan and EUR 6 million working-capital loan.
Middle East situation is extremely fluid; management has given up predicting recovery timing.
Constant-currency disclosure will continue; 11% gap in hotel GTV vs INR this quarter.
call_points.versus_prior: addressed investor request for constant-currency disclosure

call_points.text: Q1FY27 expected to be better than Q4 and same period last year, with EBITDA growth in dollar terms from both.
SG&A growth will not accelerate and will slightly taper; top line should grow faster than SG&A from here.
Expects to return to more than 100% CFO-to-EBITDA by end-FY27 as timing issues resolve.
Classic Vacations integration about halfway, targeted for completion by end of Q3 (calendar year-end).
Middle East remains below pre-war levels but is catching up; demand diversion to Europe seen.
FY27 effective tax rate expected at 18-18.5%, similar to Q4.
Debt has a one-year moratorium; repayment starts Q3FY27 and runs four years.
Air GTV back to ₹3,400 Cr organic; Q1 trajectory a shade better than Q4.
Monthly transacting buyers reached 30,063 organically in Q4FY26, up from 28,409 in Q4FY25.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The issue is wrt applicability of service tax on credit card cash back income for the period FY 2013-14, 2014-15 and from April 2015 to June 2017. The department has filed an appeal before Customs, Excise and Service Tax Appellate Tribunal, Chandigarh against the favourable order received from Commissioner Central Tax GST, Gururgram The Company awaits hearing from the CESTAT, Chandigarh on this matter.

tax_litigation.status: Hearing was held on 16 February 2026 before the CESTAT, Chandigarh on this matter; the Bench heard the submissions from both sides. The Bench is yet to pronounce the order basis the arguments filed.

tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: The issue is wrt applicability of service tax on the following for the period FY 2015-16, 2016-17 and upto June 2017: a) Commission/ Incentive (GDS/CRS) income - INR 58.03 Mn b) Income in lieu of no show of passengers in case of air travel - INR 20.02 Mn c) Income in the form of liabilities written back - INR 12.28 Mn. In relation to first two matters, the department has filed an appeal before CESTAT Chandigarh against the favourable order received from Principal Commissioner of GST. In relation to the third matter, the Company has filed an appeal before CESTAT Chandigarh against the order of Principal Commissioner of GST. tax_litigation.as_last_disclosed: This issue is wrt service tax demand raised under Section 73A(3) of the Finance Act, 1994 wherein it was alleged that service tax was collected from sub-agents without any authority of law and this tax was not deposited with the Revenue Department. operating_notes.text: FY26 standalone revenue was ₹583.8 Cr, with air ticketing ₹291.0 Cr, hotels and packages ₹97.8 Cr and others ₹195.0 Cr.
The company completed the acquisition of 100% of Classic Vacations LLC for USD 125 Mn (closing consideration USD 110.58 Mn plus USD 14.42 Mn adjustments) on October 1, 2025.
Net gain on foreign exchange differences was ₹17.24 Cr in Q4FY26, including ₹16.45 Cr unrealised on translation of non-current USD monetary assets.
Organic GTV reached ₹9,037.9 crore in Q4FY26.
Air GTV is back to ₹3,400 Cr on an organic basis.
Classic Vacations supplier relationship asset is about USD 50 Mn, amortised over 15 years.
Hotel business retail vs API mix is roughly 50:50 on GTV, with retail higher on GP.
Intercompany TBO sales to Classic were about ₹65 Cr in Q1FY27.
Classic Vacations has an 11% GP profile versus about 1% for air GTV.
North America is approaching a quarter of hotel GTV after the Classic acquisition.
ED Special Director (Adjudication) imposed a ₹22.22 Cr FEMA penalty on TBO Tek and ₹2.47 Cr on each Joint Managing Director over Section 3(c)/42(1) contravention; company reviewing options.

timeline.summary: Ankush Nijhawan, as TBO Tek Limited promoter, declared no encumbrance on shares by promoter group during FY2025-26 under SEBI Takeover Regulations.
LAP Travel Private Limited, under **Ankush Nijhawan**, declared no encumbrance on TBO Tek Limited shares for FY2025-26 under SEBI’s Regulation 31(4) on April 1, 2026.

TBO Tek Limited schedules earnings conference call for Q4 & FY 2026 results on May 29, 2026, at 15:30 IST with Mr. Ankush Nijhawan, Mr. Gaurav Bhatnagar, Mr. Akshat Verma, Mr. Vikas Jain, Mr. Pramendra Tomar, and Mr. Shreshth Mahajan.
TBO Tek reported nil deviation in the utilization of its ₹400 crore IPO proceeds for Q4FY26 on May 28, 2026.
TBO Tek released its investor presentation for Q4FY26 showcasing organic GTV of ₹9,038 crore and revenue of ₹542 crore.
TBO Tek's Q4 & FY26 earnings call (May 29, 2026) guided Q1FY27 to grow both YoY and QoQ, SG&A growth to taper, and cash flow to normalise by FY27-end.
